newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica says not seeking privileges.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica says not seeking privileges.

text.p: Telefonica is not looking to garner a privileged market position in Spain when it is fully privatised in 1997 or after the sector is opened to foreign competition in 1998, a spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday.

He denied a report in Expansion newspaper which said the firm had proposed that the government fix minimum tariffs for new competitors in Spain, and that it soften the eventual compensation to be paid to mobile telecoms operator Airtel.
The report said Telefonica de Espana SA was trying to maintain its near-monopoly.
Telefonica's chairman has written a letter to the Development Ministry seeking clarification on its share placement, tariffs, Airtel, and the government's plans for the sector, the spokesman said.
But he denied the company was trying to manipulate its position.
"Telefonica is seeking neither a privileged position nor special conditions," he said.
Spain plans to place its remaining 21 percent stake in Telefonica on the share market in early 1997.
A Development Ministry spokewoman said the department had received a letter, but she was unaware of its content.
She also said relations between Minister Rafael Arias Salgado and Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga were good, contrary to Expansion's report.
Market analysts had been concerned about the unusual call Villalonga made recently to urge the government to open the Spanish telecoms sector to international operators in 1998.

He warned that if Spain does not go ahead with liberalisation at that date, Brussels could freeze Telefonica's integration in Unisource, which could slice up to 20 percent off the value of the Spanish firm's stock.
